title: Ang 938–946: the Sidh Gosht
tomorrow: why would a Guru borrow the tune of a war ballad?
last: LETTERS, A LADDER TO THE NAME.

cards: Sooner or later every podcast guest gets the same question: who were your mentors? Ang 938 opens on that question, asked by yogis.
The Sidh Gosht, the discussion with the Siddhas: Guru Nanak among wandering yogis who had left the world behind. Tradition places them in the mountains.
They test him with question after question, about the road, the self, the way out. And then the big one: who is your guru? Whose disciple are you?

teach.b: Guru Nanak's answer, on ang 943, in paraphrase: the Shabad, the Word, is the Guru; the attention tuned to it, surat, is the disciple. Not a person on a seat. The Word.
And the one who learns isn't even the whole self; it's the listening part.

The yogis had left homes and work behind to look for truth on the heights. Guru Nanak's answer brings it back down: the Word can be heard wherever a person truly listens, in a kitchen as well as on a mountain.
It's the line under this whole walk through the Granth, and part of why the Granth itself is honored as Guru.
Now the week, page by page. Two Gurus in one raga, both signing Nanak. A hymn of many names, Ram and Khuda at one table, and the hukam beneath.
The Anand, with its party and its ease. The Sadd: sing, don't weep. The chhants, where the dear Friend stands close.
Oankar, the alphabet as a ladder.
And today, the yogis' question, answered with the Word. Seven days in Ramkali, and each turned out to be about what a person listens to.

how: Sikhs read the Sidh Gosht in Ramkali and often quote its line that the Shabad is the Guru and the attention tuned to it is the disciple; it is one reason the Granth is honored as Guru.

games.q: a friend says she can't be spiritual because she's never had a teacher. by Guru Nanak's answer to the yogis, what fits?
o: the Word itself can be the teacher; her attention is the student.
she needs to find a living guru first; the Word comes after.
teachers don't matter; whatever she feels is guidance enough.
games.why: asked 'who is your guru?', Guru Nanak answers: the Shabad, with surat, attention, as the disciple.

practice: Close your eyes and choose one sound in the room: a fan, traffic, your own breath. Give it your whole attention, the way surat leans toward the Word. When the mind wanders off, notice, and come back to the sound.
